node.label: Exponential initial value

node.label: Percent growth and decay models

node.label: Halving time
node.description: Interpret or calculate the time required for an exponentially decaying quantity to halve.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Exponential horizontal asymptote
node.description: Identify the horizontal asymptote of an exponential function graph and interpret it as limiting behaviour.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Exponential domain and range
node.description: Determine the domain and range of basic and transformed exponential functions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Exponential vertical shift and asymptote
node.description: Connect vertical shifts of exponential graphs to changes in the horizontal asymptote and range.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rewrite to common base

node.label: Logarithmic exponential form conversion
node.description: Convert between logarithmic form and exponential form to interpret and solve equations.

node.label: Log base and argument conditions
node.description: Identify valid logarithm bases and positive argument conditions in real-valued logarithmic expressions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Log product law applications
node.description: Apply the logarithm product law to combine or expand logarithmic expressions with valid arguments.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Log quotient law applications
node.description: Apply the logarithm quotient law to combine or expand logarithmic expressions with valid arguments.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Log power law applications
node.description: Apply the logarithm power law to move exponents into or out of logarithmic coefficients.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Change of base formula
node.description: Use the change of base formula to evaluate logarithms in bases not directly available on a calculator or technology tool.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Log graph as inverse of exponential
node.description: Interpret logarithmic graphs as reflections or inverses of corresponding exponential graphs under appropriate domain and range restrictions.

node.label: Log vertical asymptote and domain
node.description: Identify the vertical asymptote and domain of logarithmic graphs from their transformations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Solve exponential equations with logarithms
node.description: Use logarithms to solve exponential equations that cannot be rewritten with a common base.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Solve logarithmic equations and check domain
node.description: Solve logarithmic equations and reject solutions that violate logarithm domain restrictions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Natural base e meaning
node.description: Interpret e as the natural base for continuous growth, decay and calculus-connected exponential functions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Exponential logarithmic model parameters in context
node.description: Interpret parameters in exponential and logarithmic models using contextual units and initial or limiting behaviour.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Growth factor is a multiplier
node.description: In an exponential model, the growth or decay factor multiplies the previous value for each equal input step.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Doubling time is constant for exponential growth
node.description: In a true exponential growth model, the time required to double is constant for equal multiplicative changes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Exponential asymptote not reached
node.description: A basic exponential graph approaches its horizontal asymptote but does not reach it in the usual unrestricted model.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Change of base enables calculation
node.description: The change of base formula rewrites a logarithm in a base supported by tables, calculators or technology.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Log solutions must satisfy domain
node.description: Solutions to logarithmic equations must make every logarithm argument positive in the original equation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Growth rate confused with growth factor
node.description: Learner uses a percentage rate directly as the exponential multiplier instead of converting it to a growth or decay factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Doubling time treated as linear addition
node.description: Learner treats doubling time as a repeated additive increase rather than a multiplicative exponential pattern.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Log solution domain not checked
node.description: Learner accepts algebraic solutions to logarithmic equations without checking the original domain restrictions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Asymptote treated as intercept
node.description: Learner treats an asymptote as a point or intercept that the graph must cross.

edge.rationale: Interpreting the base as a multiplier is central to exponential function form.
Percent growth and decay models directly practise exponential growth and decay structure.
Horizontal asymptotes are core features of exponential graphs.
Converting forms directly practises logarithms as inverse exponent questions.
Change of base extends logarithm-law reasoning to equivalent logarithm forms.
Vertical asymptotes and domains are central to logarithmic graph interpretation.
Initial-value interpretation depends on recognising the parameters of exponential function form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify the starting quantity when input is zero.

edge.rationale: Base-as-factor reasoning builds on recognising constant ratios in exponential functions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the base as an additive change.

edge.rationale: Percent growth and decay modelling requires converting rates into multiplicative factors.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses 5 instead of 1.05 or 0.95 for a five percent change.

edge.rationale: Doubling time is interpreted within exponential growth contexts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expects equal additive increases over equal doubling intervals.

edge.rationale: Halving-time reasoning mirrors doubling-time reasoning for exponential decay.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats decay as subtracting a fixed amount each interval.

edge.rationale: Asymptote interpretation requires prior recognition of exponential graph features.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies the asymptote as an intercept or reachable value.

edge.rationale: The range of an exponential function is determined partly by asymptotic behaviour.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives all real values as the range for a basic exponential graph.

edge.rationale: Vertical shifts move the exponential graph's horizontal asymptote.
edge.failure_signal: Learner shifts the graph but leaves the asymptote unchanged.

edge.rationale: Common-base solving depends on recognising equivalent powers and equating exponents.
edge.failure_signal: Learner equates bases or coefficients rather than exponents after rewriting.

edge.rationale: Converting between forms depends on understanding logarithms as inverse exponent questions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner swaps base, exponent and result positions incorrectly.

edge.rationale: Logarithm conditions extend domain restrictions for logarithmic expressions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner allows zero, negative arguments or invalid bases in real-valued logarithms.

edge.rationale: Product-law application depends on knowing logarithm laws and their valid conditions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies product law to sums or invalid arguments.

edge.rationale: Quotient-law application is commonly developed alongside product-law logarithm reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses quotient order or subtracts logs with invalid arguments.

edge.rationale: Power-law reasoning extends repeated-product ideas in logarithm laws.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies the exponent to the logarithm base or argument incorrectly.

edge.rationale: Change of base follows from logarithm-law equivalence and inverse relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses numerator and denominator logs or changes only the argument base.

edge.rationale: Logarithmic graphs are interpreted as inverses of exponential graphs through graph reflection.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reflects across the wrong line or misses domain-range reversal.

edge.rationale: Logarithmic vertical asymptotes and domains are graph features of logarithmic functions.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives all real values as the domain for a basic logarithmic graph.

edge.rationale: Solving exponential equations with logs depends on converting exponential relationships into logarithmic form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot isolate the exponent when bases cannot be matched.

edge.rationale: Checking logarithmic equation solutions requires knowing valid log arguments and bases.
edge.failure_signal: Learner keeps extraneous solutions that make an original log argument nonpositive.

edge.rationale: Natural-base interpretation builds on the natural exponential function.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats e as an arbitrary variable rather than a fixed base with special modelling and calculus roles.

edge.rationale: Parameter interpretation is part of contextual exponential and logarithmic modelling.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives fitted parameters without interpreting initial value, rate, base or units.
